app-preview

A command-line tool that turns raw app screenshots and screen recordings into App Store and Google Play assets that pass store validation the first time. It works the same for developers at a terminal and for AI agents.

pipx install app-preview
app-preview generate raw/*.png -t apple.iphone-6.9 -t google.phone --template dark --caption "Plan your week"

46 store targets

Every App Store and Google Play screenshot, preview video, graphic and icon spec, from the official pages.

Validate

Size, format, transparency, color mode, file size, counts, video codec and length, each with a stable code and a fix.

Marketing screenshots

Captions, gradients and device frames that scale to every device and orientation.

Whole listings

One app-preview.yaml renders every screen × device × language.

App previews

Convert recordings or build slideshows that meet Apple's encoding rules.

Agent-ready

--json everywhere, stable exit codes, and a built-in MCP server.

Install

pipx install app-preview                 # or: uv tool install app-preview
uvx app-preview --help                   # run once without installing
pipx install "app-preview[mcp]"          # include the MCP server for AI agents
  • Python 3.10 or newer. Dependencies (Pillow, click, PyYAML, pydantic) install automatically.
  • Homebrew: brew install pipx && pipx install app-preview.
  • From source: pipx install git+https://github.com/Dev101911/AppPreviewGenerator.
  • Optional tools: ffmpeg for videos; Xcode (iOS) or adb (Android) for capture.

Check it works with app-preview --version and app-preview targets.

Quickstart

1. Pick your targets

A target is a store plus a device class. For a typical iOS and Android app, start with:

app-preview targets --store apple       # apple.iphone-6.9, apple.ipad-13, ...
app-preview targets google.phone        # full rules for one target

2. Check what you have

app-preview identify shots/home.png     # which targets does it already fit?
app-preview validate shots/*.png -t apple.iphone-6.9

3. Make compliant copies

app-preview generate shots/*.png -t apple.iphone-6.9 -t apple.ipad-13 -t google.phone -o store-assets

Files land in store-assets/<target>/01_home.png and are validated again after writing.

4. Make them look like a store listing

app-preview generate shots/home.png shots/list.png -t apple.iphone-6.9 \
  --template sunset --frame phone --caption "Plan your week" --caption "Lists that sort themselves"

5. Scale up with a config file

app-preview init        # writes a commented app-preview.yaml
app-preview build       # every screen × target × locale, validated

Core concepts

Targets

Each target records what a store accepts for one slot: exact pixel sizes (Apple) or size rules (Google), formats, whether transparency is allowed, the file-size limit, how many images a set may have, and whether templates and frames are allowed. Target IDs look like apple.iphone-6.9, apple.ipad-13-preview or google.feature-graphic. The full list is in the targets reference.

Targets have a kind:

  • screenshot: images that need exact sizes or size rules.
  • video: App Store app previews; IDs end in -preview.
  • graphic: the Play feature graphic and TV banner.
  • icon: app icons.

Validate, then generate

validate reports every problem with a file and changes nothing. generate writes new files that fit the target, then validates its own output, so a successful run means the files will be accepted. Most validation errors include a fix that is simply a generate command.

Output for people and machines

Every command prints readable text by default. Add --json and stdout carries exactly one JSON document instead. Exit codes are stable: 0 means success, 1 means validation failed, 2 means a usage or input error (details).

Store specs are data

The rules live in JSON files with their source URLs and the date they were last verified. A weekly check compares them with the stores' published pages (more).

Validating

app-preview validate shots/*.png -t apple.iphone-6.9
FAIL  shots/home.png  1179x2556 png
      error: [alpha] Image has an alpha channel; this target does not allow transparency
            fix: Run `app-preview generate shots/home.png --target apple.iphone-6.9` to produce a compliant copy.
      error: [dimensions] 1179x2556 is not an accepted size; expected one of 1320x2868, 1290x2796, ...

apple.iphone-6.9: 1 file(s), 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)

What is checked for images:

  • Size: exact pixel sizes for Apple; shortest and longest side, maximum aspect ratio and allowed aspect ratios for Google.
  • Format: PNG or JPEG, detected from the file content rather than the extension.
  • Transparency and color: no alpha channel where a store forbids it (all screenshots, App Store icons); RGB color mode.
  • Set rules: file-size limits, set counts (too many is an error, too few a warning), one size per Apple Watch set, a warning for mixed orientation.
  • Google Play promotion: warnings when you miss the 1080 px, 9:16/16:9 and 4-screenshot recommendations.

Videos get their own checks; see App preview videos. To find out which targets a file already satisfies, use app-preview identify FILE.

Generating screenshots

app-preview generate raw/*.png -t apple.iphone-6.9 -t google.phone -o out --mode fit --background auto
  • Size selection. An exact match is kept. Otherwise the tool picks the target size in the source's orientation with the closest aspect ratio, preferring the largest size. Force a size with --size 1290x2796.
  • Modes. fit letterboxes onto --background; fill scales to cover and center-crops; stretch distorts to the exact size.
  • Background. A color name, #RRGGBB, or auto, which averages the image's edge color for seamless letterboxing. It is also used to flatten transparency.
  • Output. OUT/<target>/NN_<name>.png (or .jpg with --format jpeg). Use --layout for upload-ready folders.
  • Warnings. You're warned when a source is upscaled more than 1.5× or letterboxed, which usually means a better source image would help.
  • Dry run. --dry-run reports every output without writing anything.

Templates and captions

A template puts the screenshot on a styled canvas with a caption and optional subtitle. Every size is a fraction of the canvas's shorter side, so one template works for iPhone, iPad, landscape and Google sizes alike. Captions wrap, shrink to fit, and are cut off with a warning only if they still don't fit at the minimum size.

app-preview templates                   # list built-ins
app-preview templates dark              # every setting of one template
app-preview generate shot.png -t apple.iphone-6.9 --template sunset --caption "Plan your week" --subtitle "In seconds"
TemplateLook
cleanSoft light gradient, dark bold caption on top, rounded screenshot with shadow.
darkDeep navy gradient with white caption; good for dark-mode apps.
minimalPlain white background, caption below the screenshot, no shadow.
sunsetVibrant orange-to-pink diagonal gradient with white caption.

Custom templates

Write YAML, usually extending a built-in and changing a few settings:

# brand.yaml
extends: dark
background:
  gradient: {from: "#4F46E5", to: "#0EA5E9", angle: 135}   # or {color: ...} or {image: bg.png}
caption: {color: "#FFFFFF", font: fonts/Brand-Bold.ttf, size: 0.08}
subtitle: {color: "#E0E7FF"}
caption_position: top                                        # or bottom
screenshot: {max_width: 0.8, corner_radius: 0.05, shadow: {blur: 0.03}, frame: phone}

Use it with --template brand.yaml or template: brand.yaml in the config. Relative paths (fonts, background images, frames) resolve against the file that declares them. Gradient angles follow CSS: 180 runs top to bottom and 90 left to right. All settings are listed in the template reference; app-preview schema template prints the JSON Schema.

The default font is Inter, bundled under the SIL Open Font License, so output looks the same on every machine. It covers Latin, Greek and Cyrillic; see Localization for other scripts.

Templates are refused (template_not_allowed) for targets where the store forbids added text or backgrounds: Wear OS, Android Automotive, and app icons.

Device frames

app-preview frames
app-preview generate shot.png -t apple.iphone-6.9 --frame phone --caption "Plan your week"
FrameDescription
autoPhone or tablet, chosen from the screenshot's aspect ratio
phoneModern phone with thin bezels and a Dynamic Island-style cutout
tabletTablet with even bezels

Built-in frames are drawn to fit each screenshot exactly, in portrait or landscape, so nothing is stretched or cropped. In a template you can set details:

screenshot:
  frame: {name: phone, color: "#E5E5EA", island: false}

Your own device artwork

Point frame at any PNG whose screen area is transparent, such as product bezels you have downloaded (Apple's are subject to Apple's terms and aren't bundled). The screen is found automatically by flood-filling from the image center. If that doesn't work for your image, use a small manifest:

# my-frame.yaml
image: my-phone-frame.png
screen: [72, 69, 1206, 2622]     # x, y, width, height of the screen in the PNG

A screenshot whose shape doesn't match the frame's screen is cropped to fill it, with a warning. Frames are refused for Wear OS and Android Automotive, where Google forbids them.

Project config & build

For a whole store listing, describe it once in app-preview.yaml and run app-preview build.

version: 1
out: store-screenshots
targets: [apple.iphone-6.9, apple.ipad-13, google.phone, apple.iphone-6.9-preview]
locales: [en-US, de-DE, ja-JP]
template: clean                       # name, path, or inline {extends: ..., ...}
layout: default                       # or fastlane / gpp
locale_overrides:
  ja: {caption: {font: fonts/NotoSansJP-Bold.otf}}
screens:
  - id: home
    source: shots/{locale}/home.png   # {locale}, {target}, {screen} are substituted
    caption: {en: "Plan your week", de: "Plane deine Woche", ja: "一週間をすばやく計画"}
  - id: detail
    source:                           # per-target sources; keys can be globs
      apple.ipad-*: shots/{locale}/ipad/detail.png
      default: shots/{locale}/detail.png
    caption: {default: "Every detail, one tap away"}
    template: {caption_position: bottom}   # per-screen overrides
  - id: demo
    source: recordings/demo.mov       # video sources go to *-preview targets only
    caption: {default: "See it in action"}
    start: 4
graphics:
  - target: google.feature-graphic
    title: Weekly Planner
    subtitle: {en: "Plan in seconds", de: "Plane in Sekunden"}
    icon: assets/icon.png
app-preview build --dry-run      # check the config and list every output
app-preview build                # render and validate
app-preview build -t google.phone -l de-DE --layout fastlane
  • Which screens go where. A screen applies to a target when it has a source for it of the right kind: images for screenshot targets, recordings for -preview targets.
  • Output. Files go to out/<locale>/<target>/NN_<screen>.png and each locale × target set is validated.
  • Errors up front. Mistakes are reported before anything is rendered, and every missing source file is listed at once.

Every field is in the config reference. app-preview schema config prints the JSON Schema, for editors and agents.

Localization

  • Localized text. Captions, subtitles and graphic titles accept a mapping of locale to text. A missing locale falls back to its language (de-DE → de), then to default; if neither exists you get missing_text.
  • Fonts per language. locale_overrides applies template overrides by locale or language, mainly to set fonts for scripts Inter doesn't cover. Noto fonts cover almost every language.
  • Missing glyphs are caught. If the font can't draw some characters, the output gets a warning naming them instead of silently showing boxes.
  • Right-to-left scripts. Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu are shaped and laid out right to left with libraqm (bundled with Pillow's wheels). The template's left/right alignment is mirrored, and graphics put the icon on the right.
  • CJK text, which has no spaces, wraps between characters.
  • Store locale codes. The stores spell some locales differently (ja vs ja-JP, he vs iw-IL, zh-Hans vs zh-CN). app-preview locales CODE shows each store's code, build warns about locales a store doesn't support, and the upload layouts use each store's own codes for folder names.

One-off commands take --locale for direction and shaping: app-preview generate shot.png -t apple.iphone-6.9 --caption "خطط لأسبوعك" --locale ar.

Store graphics & icons

app-preview graphic -t google.feature-graphic --title "Weekly Planner" --subtitle "Plan in seconds" --icon icon.png --template sunset
app-preview graphic -t google.tv-banner --title "Weekly Planner" --icon icon.png -o banner.png

The Play feature graphic (1024×500) and TV banner (1280×720) are built from your app name, an optional tagline and your icon, in any template's colors and fonts. Text tries to fit on one line before wrapping. The icon and text stay inside the central 80% because Google crops feature graphics in some places. In a config, list them under graphics:.

App icons are plain resizes: app-preview generate icon.png -t google.icon -t apple.icon gives a 512×512 Play icon (transparency kept) and a 1024×1024 opaque App Store icon.

App preview videos

App Store app previews are optional 15–30 second videos with strict encoding rules. These features need ffmpeg (brew install ffmpeg or apt install ffmpeg).

app-preview validate demo.mov -t apple.iphone-6.9-preview
app-preview generate demo.mov -t apple.iphone-6.9-preview -t apple.ipad-13-preview --start 3
app-preview generate demo.mov -t apple.iphone-6.9-preview --template dark --frame phone --caption "See it in action"
app-preview slideshow shots/*.png -t apple.iphone-6.9-preview --template clean --caption A --caption B --caption C

What is checked

  • Container and codec: .mp4, .mov or .m4v; H.264 up to High Profile Level 4.0, or ProRes 422 HQ in .mov.
  • Picture: an exact accepted resolution, 15–30 seconds, at most 30 fps.
  • Audio: stereo AAC (or PCM for ProRes) at 44.1 or 48 kHz. A silent track is fine; no track at all isn't.
  • Limits: 500 MB per file and up to 3 previews per device size and language.

What generate does

  • Size and frame rate. Scales to the accepted size (886×1920 for most iPhones, 1200×1600 for iPads) and caps the frame rate at 30 fps.
  • Length. Trims to 30 s; choose the segment with --start. Clips under 15 s are refused unless you pass --extend, which holds the last frame.
  • Encoding. H.264 High@4.0 at about 11 Mbps with 256 kbps stereo AAC; a silent track is added if the recording has none.
  • Vision Pro. Its previews (3840×2160) are beyond H.264 Level 4.0, so they're encoded as ProRes 422 HQ .mov.
  • Templates and frames work as for screenshots: the recording plays inside the screen area, under the caption.

slideshow turns screenshots into a preview with crossfades and fits the total into 15–30 s automatically (or set --seconds per slide). Previews show a poster frame from 5 s in by default; with fastlane, change it with deliver's preview_frame_time_code.

Google Play's promo video is a YouTube URL entered in Play Console, not an uploaded file, so there's nothing to generate for it.

Capturing screenshots

app-preview capture simulators                      # which simulator fits which Apple target
app-preview capture ios -o shots/en-US/home.png     # --device "iPhone 17 Pro Max" if several are booted
app-preview capture android -o shots/en-US/home.png # --device emulator-5554 if several are connected

Capture takes a screenshot straight from a running iOS Simulator (macOS with Xcode, via xcrun simctl) or an Android emulator or device (via adb). It first sets a clean status bar: 9:41, full battery and signal, and on Android no notifications. Each capture reports which targets it already fits.

The status bar overrides stay on so a series of shots looks consistent. Reset them with xcrun simctl status_bar booted clear or adb shell am broadcast -a com.android.systemui.demo -e command exit.

Modern Android phones are taller than Google Play's 2:1 limit, so run Android captures through generate or a template before uploading.

Upload layouts

With --layout (or layout: in the config), output goes straight into the folders your upload tool reads:

LayoutAppleGoogle
defaultout/<locale>/<target>/out/<locale>/<target>/
fastlaneout/fastlane/screenshots/<locale>/
out/fastlane/app_previews/<locale>/		out/fastlane/metadata/android/<locale>/images/phoneScreenshots/, featureGraphic.png, …
gppsame as fastlaneout/play/listings/<locale>/graphics/phone-screenshots/, feature-graphic/, …
  • Locale folders use each store's codes: ja-JP in your config becomes ja for Apple; he becomes iw-IL for Google.
  • Apple devices. deliver identifies devices by pixel size. iPad Pro 12.9" (2nd gen) files get the APP_IPAD_PRO_129 marker so they don't land in the 13" slot. Preview files are prefixed with their App Store Connect type, such as IPHONE_67_.
  • Same-size targets. Apple TV and Vision Pro share a size that deliver can't tell apart, so you get a warning; build them separately.
  • Unsupported targets. Targets an upload tool has no folder for (Chromebook, XR, Automotive, apple.icon) are skipped with a warning.
# Fastfile
deliver(screenshots_path: "out/fastlane/screenshots", app_previews_path: "out/fastlane/app_previews")
supply(metadata_path: "out/fastlane/metadata/android")

For Gradle Play Publisher, copy out/play into your app module's src/main/play.

AI agents & JSON

app-preview never prompts and is safe to run unattended. With --json, stdout is a single JSON document:

{
  "ok": false,
  "target": "apple.iphone-6.9",
  "files": [{
    "path": "shots/home.png", "ok": false, "width": 1179, "height": 2556, "format": "png",
    "issues": [{"severity": "error", "code": "dimensions",
                "message": "1179x2556 is not an accepted size; ...",
                "fix": "Run `app-preview generate shots/home.png --target apple.iphone-6.9` ..."}]
  }],
  "set_issues": [],
  "summary": {"files": 1, "errors": 1, "warnings": 0}
}

Usage and input errors use the same shape with exit code 2: {"ok": false, "error": {"code": "unknown_target", "message": "..."}}. A recommended flow for agents:

  1. app-preview targets --json to choose targets.
  2. app-preview schema config, then write app-preview.yaml.
  3. app-preview build --dry-run --json to check the config and see every output.
  4. app-preview build --json, then read ok, outputs[].warnings, warnings[] and validation[].

The repository's AGENTS.md has more recipes.

MCP server

app-preview mcp runs a stdio Model Context Protocol server that offers the same features as tools. It needs the optional extra and works with the MCP Python SDK 1.x and 2.x.

pipx install "app-preview[mcp]"
claude mcp add app-preview -- app-preview mcp          # Claude Code
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "app-preview": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["--from", "app-preview[mcp]", "app-preview", "mcp"]}
  }
}
ToolKindWhat it does
list_targetsread-onlyList store targets. kind is screenshot, graphic, icon or video. Returns compact entries; call get_target for the full spec.
get_targetread-onlyFull spec for one target: sizes or size rules, formats, transparency, limits, notes, source.
validateread-onlyCheck images or videos against a target. Every problem is reported with a stable code.
identifyread-onlyWhich targets each file already satisfies without changes.
list_templatesread-onlyBuilt-in templates with every setting; pass a name as template, or extend one.
schemaread-onlyJSON Schema for app-preview.yaml (config) or for template files (template).
localesread-onlyMap a locale (e.g. ja-JP, he) to each store's code, or list store locale codes.
generatewrites filesMake compliant copies of screenshots (or, for *-preview targets, recordings) for each target. template/captions/frame give styled marketing screenshots; captions/subtitles are one per input.
buildwrites filesRender everything in an app-preview.yaml (screens x targets x locales, plus graphics), then validate. Use dry_run=true first: it checks the config and lists all outputs.
graphicwrites filesRender a Google Play feature graphic or TV banner from a title, tagline and app icon.
slideshowwrites filesTurn screenshots into an App Store preview video (*-preview targets). Needs ffmpeg.
init_configwrites filesWrite a commented starter app-preview.yaml. Refuses to overwrite unless force=true.
capturewrites filesScreenshot a booted iOS Simulator (macOS + Xcode) or Android emulator/device (adb), with a clean status bar. Returns the targets the capture already fits.

Tools return the same JSON as --json. Errors come back as data ({"ok": false, "error": {...}}) so the agent sees the error code. Relative paths resolve against the server's working directory, so start it from your project folder.

GitHub Action

jobs:
  store-assets:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: assets
        uses: Dev101911/AppPreviewGenerator@v0
        with:
          args: build --layout fastlane      # any app-preview command line
          # install-ffmpeg: true             # for app preview videos
          # python-version: "3.12"
          # working-directory: app/
      - run: echo "ok=${{ steps.assets.outputs.ok }}, result in ${{ steps.assets.outputs.result }}"

The action installs the matching app-preview version and runs your command with --json. It writes a summary table to the job page and fails the step when validation fails. Outputs:

  • ok: "true" or "false".
  • result: the path to the JSON result.

Python API

The package installs as app-preview and is imported as apppreview (Python module names can't contain hyphens).

from apppreview import generate, generate_graphic, validate_images, identify

report = validate_images(["shot.png"], "apple.iphone-6.9")
print(report.ok, report.to_dict()["summary"])

result = generate(["shot.png"], ["apple.iphone-6.9", "google.phone"], out_dir="out",
                  template="dark", captions=["Plan your week"], frame="phone")
for output in result.outputs:
    print(output.path, output.warnings)

Builds are available as apppreview.config.build(path). Errors raise apppreview.errors.AppPreviewError, which carries .code and .message.

Commands

Every command accepts -h/--help; all but schema and mcp accept --json.

app-preview build

Render every screen x target x locale defined in CONFIG (default: app-preview.yaml).

app-preview build [OPTIONS] [CONFIG]
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
CONFIGargumentapp-preview.yaml
-t, --target repeatabletextOnly build these targets.
-l, --locale repeatabletextOnly build these locales.
--dry-runflagCheck the config and list outputs without rendering.
--layoutdefault | fastlane | gppOverride the config's layout: default, fastlane (deliver/supply) or gpp (Gradle Play Publisher).
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview build
app-preview build -t apple.iphone-6.9 -l de-DE --dry-run --json
app-preview build --layout fastlane

app-preview capture android

Screenshot an Android emulator or device over adb. Demo mode stays on until adb shell am broadcast -a com.android.systemui.demo -e command exit.

app-preview capture android [OPTIONS]
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
-o, --outpathPNG file to write.
--devicetextadb serial, if more than one device is connected.
--no-demo-modeflagLeave the status bar as is (default: demo mode, 09:41).
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview capture android -o shots/en-US/home.png

app-preview capture ios

Screenshot a booted iOS Simulator (needs Xcode). The status bar override stays until xcrun simctl status_bar booted clear.

app-preview capture ios [OPTIONS]
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
-o, --outpathPNG file to write.
--devicetextSimulator name or UDID, if more than one is booted.
--no-status-barflagLeave the status bar as is (default: 9:41, full bars).
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview capture ios -o shots/en-US/home.png --device "iPhone 17 Pro Max"

app-preview capture simulators

Which iOS simulators produce screenshots that fit each Apple target without resizing.

app-preview capture simulators [OPTIONS]
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview capture simulators

app-preview frames

List built-in device frames. Custom frames are PNGs with a transparent screen.

app-preview frames [OPTIONS]
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview frames --json

app-preview generate

Resize IMAGES into compliant screenshots for one or more targets.

Output goes to OUT/<target-id>/NN_<name>.<ext> and is re-validated. With --template or --caption, screenshots are placed on a styled canvas.

app-preview generate [OPTIONS] IMAGES...
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
IMAGESargument (repeatable)
-t, --target repeatabletextTarget ID; repeat for several.
-o, --outtextapp-preview-outOutput directory.
--modefit | fill | stretchfitfit: letterbox on background; fill: center-crop; stretch: distort.
--backgroundtext#ffffffLetterbox/flatten color: name, #RRGGBB, or 'auto' (matches the image edges).
--formatpng | jpegOutput format [default: png].
--sizetextExact output size WIDTHxHEIGHT; must be accepted by every target.
--dry-runflagReport what would be written without writing files.
--templatetextTemplate name (see app-preview templates) or template .yaml path.
--caption repeatabletextCaption per image, in order. Implies a template.
--subtitle repeatabletextSubtitle per image, in order.
--localetextLanguage of the captions (e.g. ar, ja-JP), for text direction and shaping.
--frametextDevice frame: auto, phone, tablet, or a frame .png/.yaml path. Implies a template.
--startnumberVideos: start time in seconds (output is at most 30s).
--extendflagVideos: hold the last frame to reach the 15s minimum.
--layoutdefault | fastlane | gppFolder layout: default, fastlane (deliver/supply) or gpp (Gradle Play Publisher).
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview generate raw/*.png -t apple.iphone-6.9 -t apple.ipad-13 -t google.phone -o out
app-preview generate shot.png -t apple.iphone-6.9 --template dark --frame phone --caption "Plan your week"
app-preview generate demo.mov -t apple.iphone-6.9-preview --start 3

app-preview graphic

Render a store graphic (feature graphic, TV banner) from a title and app icon.

app-preview graphic [OPTIONS]
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
-t, --targettextgoogle.feature-graphic or google.tv-banner.
--titletextMain text, usually the app name.
--subtitletextOptional tagline.
--iconpathApp icon image, shown left of the text.
--templatetextcleanTemplate for background, colors and fonts.
-o, --outtextapp-preview-outOutput file or directory.
--formatpng | jpegOutput format [default: png].
--dry-runflagReport what would be written without writing files.
--localetextLanguage of the text (e.g. ar, ja-JP), for text direction and shaping.
--layoutdefault | fastlane | gppFolder layout: default, fastlane (deliver/supply) or gpp (Gradle Play Publisher).
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview graphic -t google.feature-graphic --title "Weekly Planner" --subtitle "Plan in seconds" --icon icon.png

app-preview identify

Show which targets each image already satisfies as-is.

app-preview identify [OPTIONS] IMAGES...
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
IMAGESargument (repeatable)
--storeapple | googleOnly consider one store.
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview init

Write a starter app-preview.yaml.

app-preview init [OPTIONS] [PATH]
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
PATHargumentapp-preview.yaml
--forceflagOverwrite an existing file.
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview init
app-preview init marketing/app-preview.yaml

app-preview locales

List store locale codes, or show how LOCALE maps to each store's code.

app-preview locales [OPTIONS] [LOCALE]
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
LOCALEargument
--storeapple | googleOnly list one store's locale codes.
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview locales ja-JP
app-preview locales --store google

app-preview mcp

Run an MCP server over stdio, exposing app-preview as tools for AI agents.

Needs the extra: pip install "app-preview[mcp]".

app-preview mcp [OPTIONS]

Examples

claude mcp add app-preview -- app-preview mcp

app-preview schema

Print the JSON Schema for the config file or for templates.

app-preview schema [OPTIONS] {config|template}
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
KINDargument

Examples

app-preview schema config > app-preview.schema.json

app-preview slideshow

Turn screenshots into an app preview video with crossfades (silent audio).

app-preview slideshow [OPTIONS] IMAGES...
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
IMAGESargument (repeatable)
-t, --target repeatabletextPreview target, e.g. apple.iphone-6.9-preview.
-o, --outtextapp-preview-outOutput directory.
--secondsnumberSeconds per slide [default: fit the total into 15-30s].
--transitionnumber0.5Crossfade length in seconds.
--templatetextTemplate for every slide.
--caption repeatabletextCaption per image, in order. Implies a template.
--frametextDevice frame for every slide. Implies a template.
--localetextLanguage of the captions.
--layoutdefault | fastlane | gppFolder layout: default, fastlane or gpp.
--dry-runflagReport what would be written without writing files.
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview slideshow shots/*.png -t apple.iphone-6.9-preview --template clean --frame phone

app-preview targets

List screenshot targets, or show details for TARGET_ID.

app-preview targets [OPTIONS] [TARGET_ID]
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
TARGET_IDargument
--storeapple | googleOnly list targets for one store.
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview targets --store apple
app-preview targets apple.iphone-6.9 --json

app-preview templates

List built-in templates, or show one template's full settings.

app-preview templates [OPTIONS] [NAME]
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
NAMEargument
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview templates
app-preview templates sunset

app-preview validate

Check IMAGES against a target's store requirements.

app-preview validate [OPTIONS] IMAGES...
OptionTypeDefaultDescription
IMAGESargument (repeatable)
-t, --targettextTarget ID, e.g. apple.iphone-6.9.
--jsonflagWrite machine-readable JSON to stdout.

Examples

app-preview validate shots/*.png -t apple.iphone-6.9
app-preview validate demo.mov -t apple.iphone-6.9-preview --json

Config file reference

Fields of app-preview.yaml (JSON also works). Paths are relative to the config file. Generated from the schema that app-preview schema config prints.

FieldTypeDefaultDescription
version11
outtext"app-preview-out"Output directory, relative to the config file
targetslist of textScreenshot target IDs; see app-preview targets
localeslist of textLocale codes, e.g. en-US; empty for a single set
templatetext or mapping or nullBuilt-in template name, path to a template file, or inline template. Omit for plain resize.
mode"fit" | "fill" | "stretch""fit"Resize mode when no template is used
backgroundtext"#ffffff"Letterbox color when no template is used, or 'auto'
format"png" | "jpeg" or null
layout"default" | "fastlane" | "gpp""default"Output folder layout: default (<locale>/<target>/), fastlane (deliver + supply), or gpp (Gradle Play Publisher for Google; deliver for Apple)
default_localetext"en-US"Locale folder for fastlane/gpp layouts when locales is empty
locale_overridesmap of text or mappingTemplate overrides per locale or language, e.g. {ja: {caption: {font: fonts/NotoSansJP-Bold.otf}}}. Use it to pick fonts that cover CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, Thai, Devanagari, etc.
screenslist of Screen
screens[].idtextrequiredUsed in output file names
screens[].sourcetext or map of textrequiredSource screenshot path, relative to the config file. May use {locale}, {target} and {screen}. A mapping picks a path per target: keys are target IDs or globs like 'apple.ipad-*', plus 'default'.
screens[].captiontext or map of text or nullCaption text, or a mapping of locale -> text (falls back to language, then 'default')
screens[].subtitletext or map of text or null
screens[].templatetext or mapping or nullTemplate overrides for this screen only
screens[].startnumber0.0Video sources: start time in seconds (previews are at most 30s)
screens[].extendtrue/falsefalseVideo sources: hold the last frame to reach the 15s minimum
graphicslist of GraphicFeature graphic, TV banner, ...
graphics[].targettextrequiredA graphic target, e.g. google.feature-graphic or google.tv-banner
graphics[].titletext or map of textrequiredUsually the app name; text or a locale -> text mapping
graphics[].subtitletext or map of text or null
graphics[].icontext or nullApp icon path, relative to the config file; may use {locale}
graphics[].templatetext or mapping or nullTemplate overrides for this graphic

Issue & error codes

Validation issues

Reported per file (files[].issues) or per set (set_issues). Any error makes the result fail with exit code 1; warnings don't.

CodeSeverityMeaning
alphaerrorHas an alpha channel where transparency isn't allowed.
audioerrorVideo audio is missing, not stereo, or uses the wrong codec or sample rate.
bitratewarningVideo bit rate is well above Apple's 10–12 Mbps target.
color_modeerror / warningNot RGB (error), or an 8-bit palette image (warning).
counterror / warningMore images than allowed (error) or fewer than required (warning).
dimensionserrorPixel size, aspect ratio or min/max side isn't accepted.
durationerrorVideo is shorter than 15 s or longer than 30 s.
extension_mismatchwarningFile content and extension disagree (e.g. a JPEG named .png).
file_sizeerrorOver the store's byte limit.
formaterrorNot an accepted format or container for the target.
frame_rateerrorVideo is over 30 fps.
mixed_orientationwarningThe set mixes portrait and landscape.
mixed_sizeserrorApple Watch screenshots must all be one size.
not_founderrorFile doesn't exist.
recommended_aspectwarningNot 9:16 or 16:9, which Google Play needs for promotion.
recommended_countwarningFewer than 4 screenshots, which Google Play recommends for promotion.
recommended_sizewarningShortest side under 1080 px, which Google Play needs for promotion.
unreadableerrorNot a readable image or video.
video_codecerrorVideo codec isn't H.264 or ProRes 422 HQ.
video_profileerrorH.264 above High@4.0, or a ProRes profile other than 422 HQ.

Usage and input errors

Returned as {"ok": false, "error": {"code", "message"}} with exit code 2.

CodeMeaning
ambiguous_deviceSeveral simulators or devices are running; pass --device.
background_unreadableA template's background image can't be read.
capture_failedxcrun simctl or adb returned an error; the message includes its output.
config_not_foundNo app-preview.yaml at the given path. Run app-preview init.
ffmpeg_failedffmpeg returned an error while converting a video.
file_existsinit would overwrite an existing file; pass --force.
font_not_foundA template font path or name can't be loaded.
frame_not_allowedThe target forbids device frames (Wear OS, Automotive, app icons).
frame_not_foundA custom frame image can't be read.
input_not_foundSource files are missing. build lists every missing file at once.
input_unreadableA source file exists but isn't a readable image.
invalid_colorA color isn't a name, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA or auto.
invalid_configapp-preview.yaml doesn't match the schema; the message lists each field.
invalid_formatThe target doesn't accept the requested --format.
invalid_frameA frame image has no enclosed transparent screen, or its manifest is malformed.
invalid_layoutLayout isn't default, fastlane or gpp.
invalid_modeMode isn't fit, fill or stretch.
invalid_optionSlideshow timing can't fit 15–30 s, or another option is out of range.
invalid_size--size isn't WIDTHxHEIGHT or isn't accepted by every target.
invalid_start--start is past the end of the video.
invalid_templateA template doesn't match the schema; the message lists each field.
missing_sourceNo screen in the config has a source of the right kind for a target.
missing_textA caption or title has no text for a locale and no default.
mixed_mediaVideos go to *-preview targets and images to the others; run them separately.
no_deviceNo booted simulator or connected device (or none matches --device).
no_inputsNo input files were given.
no_output_sizeThe target has no size to generate; pass --size.
no_targetsNo --target was given.
not_a_graphic_targetgraphic only works with graphic targets (feature graphic, TV banner).
not_a_video_targetslideshow only works with *-preview targets.
nothing_to_buildThe --target/--locale filters match nothing in the config.
template_not_allowedThe target forbids added text and backgrounds (Wear OS, Automotive, icons).
template_not_foundA template file path doesn't exist.
text_count_mismatchGive exactly one --caption (and --subtitle) per input image.
too_many_imagesMore inputs than the target allows (e.g. 10 for Apple, 8 for Google).
tool_not_foundA required tool is missing: ffmpeg, xcrun, adb, or the MCP extra.
unknown_frameNot a built-in frame name or a .png/.yaml path.
unknown_targetNot a target ID; see app-preview targets.
unknown_templateNot a built-in template name or a .yaml/.json path.
unreadableffprobe can't read the video.
unsupported_in_layoutThe upload tool for this layout has no folder for the target.
video_too_shortThe clip is under 15 s; record longer or pass --extend.

Exit codes

CodeMeaning
0Success; everything validated (warnings allowed).
1Validation failed: at least one error-level issue.
2Usage or input error: unknown target, missing file, bad option, missing tool.

Keeping specs current

Apple and Google change their requirements; Apple recently added iPhone Duo sizes, for example. The rules live in src/apppreview/data/ with their source and verified date, and a scheduled workflow runs python -m apppreview.speccheck every Monday. It checks:

  • Apple screenshot sizes: every size on the page must be in the data, and vice versa.
  • App preview sizes: every accepted preview size must still be listed.
  • Locale codes: both stores' lists must match.
  • Wording: a fingerprint of each page's text, which catches rule changes such as a new count limit.

When something changes it opens a "Store specs changed" issue. CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to update the data.

Troubleshooting

Text shows as boxes

The font has no glyphs for that language; the output warning lists the characters. Set a font for that locale with locale_overrides (for example Noto Sans JP for Japanese).

"Screenshot is upscaled" warnings

The source is much smaller than the target. Capture from a larger simulator (app-preview capture simulators suggests one) or accept slightly softer output.

My Android screenshots fail dimensions

Phones taller than 2:1 exceed Google Play's aspect limit. Use generate with --mode fit or a template; both produce 1080×1920.

tool_not_found

Install the named tool: ffmpeg for videos, Xcode for capture ios, Android platform-tools (adb) for capture android, or app-preview[mcp] for the MCP server.

Right-to-left text isn't shaped

Your Pillow build lacks libraqm. Pillow's official wheels include it; reinstall with pip install --force-reinstall pillow, or on Homebrew run brew install libraqm.

deliver puts screenshots in the wrong device slot

deliver goes by pixel size. Don't mix targets that share a size (Apple TV and Vision Pro) in one upload; build warns when that happens.
